key_insight: A recursive deep-learning pipeline can replace slow finite-element simulation to predict the full transverse-compression response of synthetic plant fibers and estimate their effective stiffness.
engineering_relevance: This enables high-throughput mechanical characterization of variable natural-fiber microstructures, supporting faster design of sustainable fiber-reinforced composites.
method: Train two coupled recursive U-Nets to propagate deformation and stress fields step by step under transverse compression.
Use a regression CNN on the final stress field to predict transverse Young’s modulus.
Train and validate on 1,000 synthetic hemp-like fiber geometries with FE ground truth, including cases with and without a lumen.
evidence_signal: The model achieved SSIM 0.9574 ± 0.0074 and RMSE 0.0345 ± 0.0079 for stress-field evolution, and predicted Young’s modulus with R² = 0.938 ± 0.024, MAE = 24.31 ± 1.23 MPa, and MAPE = 5.25 ± 0.91%, while inference took under one second versus about five minutes for FE.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on synthetic geometries derived from hemp cross-sections, so robustness on unseen real fibers, broader loading conditions, or manufacturing variability still needs validation.
paper_title: Deep Learning-based Mechanical Characterization of Synthetically Generated Plant Fibers under Transverse Compression
